en: Would you like to take a rest?
You awake feeling refreshed.
You settle down beside the campfire and gaze into the flames.

As you enter the room, many bloody eyes turn to rest on you. At the center, upon a blood-red plush throne sits a man whose pallid flesh is framed in ostentatious finery. He makes no effort to conceal his fangs, and he regards you with cold amusement. This can only be Frico.
Byrne says nothing, but he clenches his fists, and his eyes are full of hate.
Byrne watches with great satisfaction as you urinate on the undignified smear that used to be Frico.
Frico regards you cooly for a moment, running his tongue idly against the tip of one of his prominent fangs.
Grant balls his fists, a low growl escaping from his throat. His muscles swell and he grows nearly a foot in height, as he pushes his body partway toward the lycanthropic monster.
Grant stands up to his full height and puts on a serious face.
Grant takes a deep breath and sighs loudly, rubbing a hand idly over his belly. Though the battle is over, Frico's taunting clearly got to him.
He looks up at you and smiles a little.
He sighs and looks at the smear on the floor.
How do you respond?
Of course, once you step into the foyer proper, the doors slam shut behind you.
Pay Frico 10,000$?
The Vampire lord Frico is no more. Now there's naught but to take his key and leave.
The room goes oddly quiet but for a hissing sound, as Frico's remains blister and crackle, the ancient vampire's body dissolving into an unsightly smear of rot and long-stagnant blood.
There is a long, pregnant pause before Frico speaks.
There is no need to return to Frico's court. You got what you came for.
This grate appears to be connected to a dumping chute from somewhere above. It is not large enough to climb through.
This grate appears to be connected to a large opening in the ceiling. It might be large enough for a person to fit through.
You came here for Frico's Key. You can't leave without it.
You do not encounter any guards, and the door appears to be wide open. It is difficult to determine whether this is an invitation, or neglect.
You do not have the money Frico is asking for, and his voice immediately takes on an annoyed tone.
You draw your weapons, and a coy sneer creeps across Frico's face.
You head down the long marble corridor toward the heart of Frico's castle.
You leave the carnage of Frico's court behind you, your key to the eastern lands firmly in hand.
You refuse Frico's price, and he narrows his eyes at you in irritation.

A trait such as "Luxalign" or "Rexalign" indicates that the creature is resistant to that particular vein, and vulnerable to that vein's opposites. Multiple alignments are cumulative, and can exacerbate or cancel one another.

A trait such as "Maxsoul" or "Luxsoul" combines the effects of an Align and a Mana trait, indicating both the creature's resistances and their natural ability to cast pure vein spells when others would normally cast Arcus.

A trait such as "Poxmana" or "Nixmana" is usually reserved for equipment, indicating that the user will be able to cast a pure vein spell instead of Arcus. Using multiple mana sources results in a collapse back to Arcus.
All incoming damage is increased by fifty percent while suffering from a fumble. If you're unlucky, one solid hit could easily kill a fumbling character outright. This is, of course, best avoided.

An enemy who realizes that the fight is going poorly may sometimes hesitate. Hesitation is only momentary, but it provides an excellent opportunity to end the combat through negotiation instead of violence.

Arcus is the Null Vein.

It is the simplest form of impure magic, and also the most flexible.

At higher levels, the ability "Imarcus" can allow a Blaster to heal allies at a great distance, and the truly powerful can learn "Arximum", which allows the Blaster to attack entire groups of foes all at once.

Bandmates all contribute to manpower in slightly different ways depending on their alignment. For most people, putting points into utility-based traits is the best way to improve manpower contributions.

Chaotic people, on the other hand, don't much care to be made into workhorses. They will contribute to manpower whether they have utilitarian skills or not, but they will each do so in their own way, and not always in the same way.
Defending yourself in combat can greatly improve your odds of survival. All incoming damage will be reduced by half while you remain in defensive stance.

Different from a magical alignment, personal alignment falls in one of three ranges - Lawful, Neutral, or Chaotic. 

Alignment comes into play in two major ways.

Everybody can defend, but defensive stance can be further improved with many skills from the Guard, Dodge, and Ward specializations to include effects such as increased dodge chance or even healing yourself and nearby allies.
If someone in the party is the only representative of their particular alignment, they miss out on this comraderie bonus.

If you learn to use Blast magic, you will almost certainly begin by using Arcus. 

There are no creatures whose souls embody Arcus, so it is moderately effective against any opponent.

Invulnerability cannot be brought down until it expires on its own after one full combat round. Of course, the same is true for invulnerable enemies, so if you encounter any, you'll have to grit your teeth and wait it out.

It is also possible, however, to fully maximize your risk without fumbling. If you're lucky enough to do this, you'll enjoy all of the benefits of defensive stance until your next turn, as well as a large bonus to the party's experience award!
Lastly, remember that Arcus exists in a space between the pure veins. Attempting to combine pure veins of magic will always result in Arcus.
Lay down an offering of gold to prove your commitment to the struggle.

Lux is the Vibrant Vein.

It is radiance and judgement, and it infuses the souls of the innocent and the divine. Those aligned strongly with Pox or Max will take additional damage from Lux.

Max is the Violent Vein.

It is raw power and overwhelming, indiscriminate destruction. It infuses the souls of demons and werebeasts. Those aligned strongly with Lux or Nix will take additional damage from Max.
Nightmarish and Alluring auras have all the same affects as an unsettling aura, but they can also sometimes cause enemies to fumble outright, even when they aren't acting recklessly!

Nix is the Variant Vein.

It is chaos and impermanence, and it infuses the souls of hybrids and shapeshifters. Those aligned strongly with Max or Rex will take additional damage from Nix.
Normal actions end your turn, but they are not subject to risk, so they are best used to cap off a chain of reckless actions.
Note that chaotic people will never reduce their manpower contributions this way, however, so don't worry that their whims will leave you shortstaffed in a pinch.
Note that invulnerability does not prevent ongoing damage from poison or from equipment with the wasting trait.

Pox is the Virulent Vein.

It is entropy and decay, and it infuses the souls of the unclean and the undying. Those aligned strongly with Rex or Lux will take additional damage from Pox.
Putting points into defensive specializations grants extra hit points as well, so don't forget to invest a little effort in defense for anyone you expect to go toe-to-toe with ogres or archdemons.
Reckless attacks can grant you extra actions in combat, but each reckless action piles on a little more risk, and risk can cause reckless actions to fail, forcing you into a fumble.

Rex is the Verdant Vein.

It is growth, energy, and life, and it infuses the souls of plants and animals. Those aligned strongly with Nix or Pox will take additional damage from Rex.
So be it. Struggle anew. Live anew.
Some creatures may offer ransom items that you may find difficult to acquire elsewhere, and some kinds of creatures make powerful allies, with special powers that no human or orc can duplicate.
Some enemies have auras that will adversely affect creatures around them. Auras are indiscriminate and apply to allies and enemies equally, so they can sometimes be difficult to manage.
Some who are truly devoted to their defensive training can achieve brief states of invulnerability in combat.
Someone with a soul trait can still use another pure vein if they have an appropriate mana focus. That is, someone with "Nixsoul" could still make use of a "Rexmana" focus to cast Rex.

The Luxic boon is "Grace".

The graceful will find their weapons guided by an invisible hand, and will rarely miss their enemies in combat.

The Luxic curse is "Daze". 

The dazed will find it difficult to focus, and will often miss when they act in combat.

The Maxic boon is "Rage".

The enraged will stagger their foes with overwhelming force, mounting their enemies' risk and forcing the careless to fumble.

The Maxic curse is "Pain". 

Those afflicted by pain take more damage from attacks, and are resistant to all forms of healing.

The Nixic boon is "Focus".

The focused will inflict more damage against enemies when casting spells.

The Nixic curse is "Nexus". 

Those under a nexus will be torn apart more easily by magic, and they will be unable to ward effectively.

The Poxic boon is "Shadowcloak".

The cloaked are difficult to see, and will often be able to avoid enemy attacks and magic.

The Poxic curse is "Poison". 

Poison will slowly kill the afflicted, draining their life away drop by drop.

The Rexic boon is "Vigor".

The envigorated are infused with simple strength, and will cause extra damage with their weapons in combat.

The Rexic curse is "Entangle". 

The entangled will find it difficult to move, which limits both their movement speed and their ability to dodge in combat.
The first place alignment matters is in determining your band's manpower. It is essential to keep manpower up if you expect to recruit more people, claim better strongholds, and retain many services.
The key is to minimize your own chance of fumbling while taking advantage of enemy fumbles. Use your level of risk to determine whether or not to act recklessly.
The second way alignment comes into play is in determining comraderie. Any combatant who has a bandmate of the same alignment in the party will be more likely to succeed when risk is high.
There are various traits that indicate a connection with one of the pure veins.

There may be times, however, when you find that one of the five pure veins is more effective against a particular foe. There exist focusing items that can refine the mana of one's blasts into a purer form, and this also allows access to curses and boons unique to the pure veins.
These traits also yield many useful skills, including improvements to hit points, carrying capacity, and visibility.

To struggle is to live. 

To sacrifice everything, to begin the struggle anew, is to appreciate one's life anew.
Violent auras are obvious, and cause damage to nearby creatures. More subtle, unsettling auras cause nearby creatures to accumulate risk every time they begin a new action.

What's more, negotiation yields the same amount of experience that you would gain by slaying the creature. There are no guarantees of success, however, and of course, if you prefer straightforward violence, you can still use a reckless attack against a hesitating enemy.
While you are invulnerable all attacks against you will fail.

You may release the hesitating enemy from combat outright, or if you share common language, you may demand an item as ransom for the creature's life, or attempt to press the creature into joining you.
Your best bet when dealing with auras is to maintain a little distance, whether the aura's source is friend or foe.
Your body and mind have been stripped clean, in order that you may rediscover yourself.
Among the bones picked clean by beasts, you find a note with some kind of code written on it. Every other entry is blank, as though code were deliberately split in half.
It seems as though this console requires a code. The keypad is far too complex for you to blindly guess it.
Rummaging through the items on the counter, you find ring of keys.
The console is unresponsive, and the badly-damaged node nearby seems to be the culprit. You'll need to repair the node before this console will operate.
The empty chest has been roughly abused, clearly having been forced open with a chisel and blunt trauma.
The lid of this chest is nowhere to be seen. The contents are likewise long gone.
The wall crumbles to reveal the lobby of the vault.
The wall here is in poor condition, evidently damage suffered from multiple break-in attempts. A bit of well-applied muscle or magic might finish the job.
There are some badly damaged wires in this node. You might be able to get it working again if you could somehow replace them.

These bare bones have been here for a long time, and judging by the condition of the clothes, this person was stabbed in the back. Rummaging through the pockets, you find a folded note with half of a code written on it.
This chest is full of random salvaged mechanical parts and wires. Nothing valuable catches your eye.
This stinking pile of bones is all that remains of whatever was being fed to the resident beast. A brief search yields nothing of interest.
You find a note inside the dusty chest that reads: "Madam Johan, if you are reading this, you may consider your outstanding debt paid in full. -B"

You find a single note pinned by a menacing looking knife with the following message scrawled: "You bastard, Regar, this was only half the payment promised. If you value your pretty little face, you'll have the rest of the payment next time we meet."
You should be able to repair this console with the coil of wire you found earlier.
You spy a length of wire that may be suitable for repairing the damaged node you found earlier.
A closer inspection reveals a lever on the bottom of this chest. It is well-disguised, so whoever looted the chest probably missed it.
A closer inspection reveals that this chest is only mostly empty. In the bottom are the dusty leftovers of a severed hand, still gripping a lever seated inside the chest.
A quick flash of a blade, and there is blood gushing from a wound in your hand. You'll have to do better than that.
Give Glamig the hairbrush?
Glamig's form begins to shiver and fade.
She holds out her hands and keeps repeating herself through desperate sobbing. She seems to want something, but not all of her speech is orcish, so it's unclear what she is asking for.
The decorations on this sarcophagus indicate that it belonged to a member of Glamig's personal guard. It appears to be empty and unused.
The decorations on this sarcophagus indicate that it belonged to a member of Glamig's personal guard. It appears to be empty.
The decorations on this sarcophagus indicate that it belonged to a member of Glamig's personal guard. It is damaged, and obviously empty.
The decorations on this sarcophagus indicate that it belonged to a member of Glamig's personal guard. There is nothing inside, however.

The image of the battered woman unravels to reveal a stately matriarch in glittering finery, surely a kinder reminder of what Glamig looked like during her life. She smiles and speaks with a voice like a thousand relieved sighs.
The markings on this sarcophagus do not give any particular clues as to who is entombed here.
The markings on this sarcophagus indicate the resting place of a personal handmaid. It appears, however, that there is no corpse inside.
The markings on this sarcophagus indicate the resting place of a personal handmaid. It is vacant.
The markings on this sarcophagus indicate the resting place of a personal handmaid. Nothing is inside.
The markings on this sarcophagus indicate the resting place of a personal handmaid. The lid is slightly ajar, showing a clean, empty interior.
The quivering, ghostly figure of the long-dead orc queen Glamig hangs in the air before you.
The trap that severed the hand has long since rusted into uselessness, and you are able to pull the lever without incident.
There is a trap here, but it is fairly obvious and easy to subvert. You pull the lever without issue.
This chest appears to have a trap on it.
This empty sarcophagus belongs to a member of Glamig's extended family. An engraving here reads "QSSI".
This empty sarcophagus belongs to a member of Glamig's extended family. An engraving reads "DLRO".
This empty sarcophagus belongs to a member of Glamig's extended family. An engraving reads "WEHT".
This empty sarcophagus belongs to a member of Glamig's extended family. The name has been chiseled off.
This empty sarcophagus belongs to a member of Glamig's extended family. The name is illegible.
This empty sarcophagus belongs to a member of Glamig's extended family. The name is worn away and cannot be read.
This empty sarcophagus belongs to a member of Glamig's extended family. The name reads "Lingun Cosova, Duchess of Babe".
This empty sarcophagus belongs to a member of Glamig's extended family. The name reads "Luc Beauregard".
This empty sarcophagus belongs to a member of Glamig's extended family. The name reads "Phara Cosova, Queen Mother".
This empty sarcophagus belongs to a member of Glamig's extended family. The name reads "Ryke Tsarath, Duke of Knavewood".
This empty sarcophagus belongs to a member of Glamig's extended family. There is an engraving that reads "ERAU".
This sarcophagus belongs to Glamig's prime minister, Fastad Nostes. There is a slight draft coming from beneath it.

Though her eyes are naught but hollows in her twisted face, you feel as though she is looking at you and trying to speak. Her voice starts like a thousand gibbering whispers and rises to a desperate plea.
Though you would expect a royal bearing, she has anything but. She is naked and shows signs of having been beaten, and her face is a twisted charicature of anger and desperate shame.
With the Queen's blessing, you open the sarcophagus. Without disturbing her body, you take the crown that was laid upon her chest.
You disarm the trap and open the chest.
You respectfully present the hairbrush to Glamig, and she takes it from you with a quivering hand.
You wait for a few long moments while Beauregard pays his respects.
These appear to be supplies the bandits were using.
"Call me a "broad" again and I'll wound more than your soul."
As you step warily into the town, a powerfully-built man with wild hair steps toward you.
He appears to be extremely upset. Maybe you should give him a moment.
He looks up and over at the man standing by the water's edge.
He looks utterly defeated.
It reads : "No shirt, no shorts, no problem. Come on in."
The guard returns to his post and makes a welcoming gesture.
The guard spends a moment giving you a brief on the town's layout.
This man appears to be upset by something, and when you approach him, he can hardly wait to get your input.
This man appears to be upset by something, but when you approach him, he stands up straight and stares at you.
This man sees you coming from a short distance away, and he visibly trembles as Rangda approaches him.
Zantanak says nothing, only flashing an unsettling grin.
"I'll need to close up soon before it gets too dark, but I've still got one last platter of sandwiches here."

He's too busy laying into a slab of honey-glazed
ham to pay any attention.
If your party is still inside the maze, you can wait for them to get here.
If your party is still inside the maze, you can wait here for them to return.
It looks like somebody got to this chest already.
Take a closer look?
The water in the fountain lies perfectly still. Even in this light, you can see your reflection in its pristine surface.
This chest is absolutely stuffed with prizes. It almost looks like there's more in here than you can carry right now.
What would you like to do?
Would you like to open the chest?

You can see small chunks of food
littered around the skeleton's feet.
It looks as though you could probably roll this boulder a few feet if you pushed it hard enough.
That boulder is a lot heavier than it looks. You'll have to give it another try.
The boulder tumbles into the water with a splash.
The switch is loose, and flipping it doesn't do anything. It seems like the mechanism is broken.
There is a note scrawled on the nearby table. Read it?
This boulder is positioned at the edge of the water. With a big enough push, it would probably slide in.
This switch appears to be seized, but the nearby gate is already open.
This switch is loose, as though it is not connected to anything.
With a mighty heave, the boulder rolls over onto its side and settles into its new position.
You find a sack of coins tucked behind this bush!
You push as hard as you can, but you can't manage to roll the boulder out of its resting place. You might have better luck with another attempt.
You root through the corpse's belongings and make a mental note not to drink the water.
Nazar can't do anything but lean on his sword and laugh.
When he finally catches his breath and looks up, he has tears in his eyes.
It reads : If you are not of the hive, you do not belong here. Begone.
The chunk of slag you are carrying comes to mind. Will you place the Wasp Soul upon the pedestal?
This crude pedestal has a warning written on the top of it.
You decide to hold on to the Wasp Soul for now. Perhaps it can be of use elsewhere.
You make an offering of the Wasp Soul, a bit of slag forged from the destruction of many weapons.
A basket of complimentary bread rolls sits on the table.
A variety of unusual dishes line the table. One stands out as being particularly tasty--a bowl of pasta in a tomato and vegetable sauce with poached eggs.
A very old loaf of bread sits atop the nightstand. It looks as if it's almost become fused with the wood...
However, you can see one particular item of clothing which takes your fancy just enough to want to fish it out.
It could be messy, but do you want to take it with you?
Leaning over the counter to check if anyone is there, you notice a single key hanging from a small hook.
Shouldn't have looked...
Somebody left a delicious, succulent... moist, warm, tender chicken here.
Someone appears to have run up a long bill for room service. One of the dishes remains untouched, but it looks good.
Take the keyring with you?
Take they keyring with you?
Thankfully, there is nothing inside.
The cabinet is filled with neatly stacked papers and assorted bits of stationery. In a corner, you see a keyring with a tag which reads "Exec. Suites".
The key is within easy reach. Do you take it?
The lantern on this table appears to be broken.
The lantern on this table appears to be broken. There is a keyring tucked beside it.
There are a couple of handy items in the chest. Perhaps the previous guest forgot to take these with them?
There is a lovely, fresh smell coming from this cabinet. It's filled with neatly folded towels and assorted toiletries.
There is a perfectly good sandwich here. It would be a shame to let it go to waste.
This cabinet is filled with laundry which has yet to be washed.
This chest is absolutely full of coins! There must hundreds of them.
This might be one to pass up.
Upon closer inspection, most of them are either rusted over or poorly minted...
Would you like to take it with you?
You take some time to sift through them a little, and find a few acceptable gold pieces.
You wait a short while, but there is no response.
Images of the surrounding area glitter in the facets of this ice crystal.
The touch of a warm hand shatters the fragile formation, but a moment later it reforms in a slightly different configuration, unique as a flake of fallen snow.
Inside the chest is a molded velvet casing for what looks to have been some sort of scepter, but it is empty.
Inside the chest, sitting in its velvet casing, is a magnificent gilded hammer, thrumming with warm, soothing energy.
Make an offering of the Paladin Soul?
There is a click when you open the chest. You brace yourself for some sort of trap, but nothing happens.
Pull the switch?
The switch broke entirely off. You won't be able to switch it back.
Upon looking closely at this bookshelf, you find a trick switch deep in the back.

He grows animated, his eyes wide.  "We've just made history! Nobody's ever accomplished such a thing before! I'll have to revise my method and figure out how to strengthen the braid. I've got a lot of work ahead of me, but I would not have come this far without your help. Take the ring with my thanks!"
He holds out the ring to show you. It is a large, gaudy thing.
The polish brings out the swirling patterns in the stone's layers, and it is a truly striking piece of jewelry.
The polished stone has taken on a deep, warm hue that accents the gold beautifully.
The smith looks up at you, sharp eyes peering up from beneath singed eyebrows, gleaming tusks jutting from a wiry beard. The old orc doesn't do a lot of socializing, it would seem.
The smith presents you with a finely crafted gold ring set with a faceted and polished stone cut from the bezoar you gave him.
The smith presents you with a magnificent gold belt buckle set with a large polished slab of the bezoar you provided.
The smith winks and waltzes back over to his furnace.
There is a wild glint in his eyes as he continues, "...unless you'd like to help with a little project of mine."
This shelf appears to be full of books on complex arcane theories.
Though sleep is not an option, you take the opportunity to relax. The smith is hard at work for a few hours, as he predicted.
